claims: The Selective Service System will automatically register eligible men (citizens and residents aged 18–25) for the military draft starting in December 2026 using existing federal data.
The automatic registration change is part of the fiscal 2026 National Defense Authorization Act.
The automatic registration change removes the need for individual self-registration.
The responsibility for registration shifts from individuals to the Selective Service System.
The Selective Service System will pull data from other federal agencies.
Almost all male U.S. citizens between 18 and 25 years old are affected.
Male immigrants residing in the U.S. between 18 and 25 years old are affected.
The automatic registration is not a reinstatement of the draft.
Reinstatement of the draft requires congressional and presidential authorization.
Registration is still mandatory by law.
Failure to be registered (even if automatic registration fails) can result in the loss of federal student loans.
Failure to be registered (even if automatic registration fails) can result in the loss of jobs.
Failure to be registered (even if automatic registration fails) can result in the loss of citizenship opportunities.
The potential military draft database has seen declining registration rates
